frozen_question: What Egyptian words underlie Meeks' translation 'un vagin en métal' in Papyrus Brooklyn 47.218.84 XI,11-XII,1, and do they designate a literal anatomical vagina, a shaped receptacle/container/matrix, or another ritual object class?

method_execution.TOPA_SPIDER: Crawl from modern quotations back to Meeks 2006, TLA, ORAEC/AES and token/lemma controls.
method_execution.FIVE_D_SPIRAL: wording -> lexeme -> material -> object ontology -> ritual function -> contradiction return
method_execution.BEETLE_GRAZER: Deduplicate Meeks-derived quotations; repetitions of the same passage are one source family.
method_execution.TENET_REVERSE: Trace later container/matrix interpretations backward to the Saite text without treating the interpretation as the original wording.
method_execution.boundary: JANUS methods organize evidence only; authority remains with the ancient text, scholarly edition, lexicon and independently checkable object evidence.

secure_passage.date_context: Saite/26th Dynasty Delta mythographic manual; pre-Plutarch Egyptian witness.
secure_passage.meeks_french_translation: Les êtres sont placés sur le djed, un vagin en métal près de lui, car les deux soeurs sont à proximité du phallus.
secure_passage.source: Dimitri Meeks, Mythes et légendes du Delta d'après le papyrus Brooklyn 47.218.84, MIFAO 125, 2006, esp. p.25 and plate/transcription references; quotation independently reproduced in Museo Egizio scholarship.

phallus.boundary: The lexeme itself is securely phallic; exact token-to-column alignment should still be preserved explicitly in any future diplomatic edition audit.

vagina.secure_level: Meeks' French translation 'vagin' is secure; the exact underlying pBrooklyn token/lemma has not yet been independently aligned in the current run.

comparative_candidate.meaning: vagina in separate Esna/Dendera/Edfu lexical discussions

vagina.forbidden_inference: Do not silently replace Meeks' translated noun with kꜣt until the pBrooklyn token is directly demonstrated.

metal.secure_level: The material adjective/noun 'en métal' is secure in Meeks' translation; the exact Egyptian metal lexeme for XI,11 was not independently isolated in the current run.
metal.forbidden_inference: Do not substitute generic Egyptian metal terms such as bjꜣ without direct token alignment.

cross_controls.spieser: Treats the metallic female form as plausibly vessel/container/matrix-like and notes a female counterpart in the Mendes resurrection complex; this is interpretation, not the underlying lexeme itself.
cross_controls.dendera: Later Osirian relic processions use vessels/containers for bodily relic geography, supporting a ritual-container object class in general but not proving the identity of the pBrooklyn metal vagina.
cross_controls.insertable_phallus_figures: Separate Ptolemaic object class proves detachable/insertion technology existed; it does not establish the engineering of the pBrooklyn female matrix.
